_comment: Copy this to the root of a repository as .ste-writing.json to switch STE on
for that repository. The file does two jobs: it is the opt-in switch the
Stop hook looks for, and it holds this project's settings.
Commit it. The glossary is a project asset, and someone who clones the
repository should get the opt-in and the technical nouns together.
Delete the file to opt out. Nothing else has to change.
_mode_comment: ste-general  READMEs, pull requests, docs, release notes. Structure rules
and the slop list. No dictionary lockdown, so ordinary words
ste-strict   Procedures, runbooks, safety text, error messages. Adds the
approved-word allowlist: every word must be in the STE
dictionary or in the glossary below.
_glossary_comment: Technical nouns, per rules 1.6 and 1.8. In ste-strict a word that is not in
the STE dictionary fails unless it is listed here. Above is a starting set
for software work. Add your own product and domain nouns.
For a long list, use "glossary_file" instead and point it at a text file of
one word per line, relative to this file.
_one_name_comment: Rule 1.11. Each key is the name to use, and its list holds the names that
should be replaced by it. A word cannot be in both this list and the
glossary above. Replace these examples with your own pairs.
